MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Round 694 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 600
   B. 680
   C. 700
   D. 690

2. In the number 6,092, the digit 6 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Tens
   B. Thousands
   C. Ones
   D. Hundreds

3. Which of these shows 718 in words? (1 mark)
   A. seven hundred and eighty-one
   B. seven hundred and twenty-eight
   C. seven hundred and eighteen
   D. eight hundred and eighteen

4. In the number 91,724, the digit 9 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Ten thousands
   B. Tens
   C. Hundreds
   D. Ones

5. Work out 6,120 − 3,845. (1 mark)
   A. 2,285
   B. 3,725
   C. 2,175
   D. 2,275

6. Estimate 38 × 22 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 8,000
   B. 800
   C. 900
   D. 700

7. Change 23/6 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 3 5/6
   B. 4 5/6
   C. 3 6/6
   D. 5 3/6

8. Which is the smallest number: 0.4, 0.44, 0.04, 0.404? (1 mark)
   A. 0.04
   B. 0.44
   C. 0.404
   D. 0.4

9. Which decimal is equal to 0.7? (1 mark)
   A. 0.70
   B. 0.07
   C. 0.71
   D. 7.0

10. A hundred square has 7 of its small squares shaded. Which decimal shows the shaded part? (1 mark)
   A. 0.7
   B. 7
   C. 0.07
   D. 0.007

11. Which expression shows "n subtracted from 20"? (1 mark)
   A. 20 + n
   B. 20 − n
   C. n − 20
   D. 20n

12. A rope 9 m 60 cm long is cut into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece? (1 mark)
   A. 4 m 80 cm
   B. 9 m 56 cm
   C. 2 m 40 cm
   D. 2 m 50 cm

13. What is 2 m 90 cm + 3 m 30 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 7 m 20 cm
   B. 5 m 20 cm
   C. 6 m 10 cm
   D. 6 m 20 cm

14. A pencil starts at the 2 cm mark on a ruler and ends at the 9 cm mark. How long is the pencil? (1 mark)
   A. 8 cm
   B. 11 cm
   C. 9 cm
   D. 7 cm

15. Change 3 m to centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 3,000 cm
   B. 300 cm
   C. 30 cm
   D. 3 cm

16. A cuboid is 3 blocks long, 3 blocks wide and 3 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 27 blocks
   B. 24 blocks
   C. 30 blocks
   D. 9 blocks

17. When we stack blocks to make a cuboid, what do we do first? (1 mark)
   A. Make one flat layer with rows and columns
   B. Put all the blocks in one long line only
   C. Count the corners of the room
   D. Cut the blocks into halves

18. One layer of a cuboid has 20 blocks and there are 4 layers. What is the volume? (1 mark)
   A. 100 blocks
   B. 76 blocks
   C. 24 blocks
   D. 80 blocks

19. A cuboid has a volume of 72 blocks. One layer has 24 blocks. How many layers are there? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 96
   C. 4
   D. 48

20. What is 4 1/2 kg + 2 3/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 7 3/4 kg
   B. 7 1/2 kg
   C. 7 1/4 kg
   D. 7 kg

21. Which unit do we use to measure the mass of a bag of maize flour? (1 mark)
   A. Centimetre
   B. Metre
   C. Litre
   D. Kilogram

22. How many minutes are in 12 hours? (1 mark)
   A. 288 minutes
   B. 1200 minutes
   C. 780 minutes
   D. 720 minutes

23. How many hours are in 5 days? (1 mark)
   A. 120 hours
   B. 300 hours
   C. 144 hours
   D. 60 hours

24. Change 270 minutes to hours and minutes. (1 mark)
   A. 4 h
   B. 5 h 30 min
   C. 4 h 30 min
   D. 5 h

25. What is 4 h 10 min − 1 h 40 min? (1 mark)
   A. 2 h 30 min
   B. 3 h 30 min
   C. 2 h 40 min
   D. 2 h 20 min

26. How many cents are in Ksh 3? (1 mark)
   A. 30 cents
   B. 3,000 cents
   C. 300 cents
   D. 103 cents

27. 325 cents is the same as (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 3.25
   B. Ksh 4.25
   C. Ksh 0.32
   D. Ksh 32.50

28. The table shows the favourite sports of 10 pupils: football 5, netball 3, athletics 1, swimming 1. What is the total of all the numbers? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 12
   C. 10
   D. 11

29. In a tally chart, 2 groups of five and 2 more single tally marks are drawn. What number do they show? (1 mark)
   A. 12
   B. 17
   C. 11
   D. 13

30. In a table, a row goes (1 mark)
   A. across the page
   B. diagonally only
   C. round in a circle
   D. down the page

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Draw a rectangle of 3 rows and 5 columns of squares. Write its area. (3 marks)

32. At what times on a clock do the hands make a right angle and a straight line? Give one example of each. (4 marks)

33. Write the four facts that belong to an array of 3 rows with 8 dots in each row. (4 marks)

34. A 20 L jerrycan is used to fill 5 L buckets. How many buckets can be filled? How many 1/4 L cups can be filled from one bucket? (4 marks)

35. Change 11/4 to a mixed fraction and then change your answer back to an improper fraction to check it. (4 marks)

36. A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. Draw it roughly, label the sides and find its perimeter. (3 marks)

37. Arrange these prices from the cheapest to the most expensive: Ksh 8.25, Ksh 8.05, Ksh 8.50, Ksh 7.99. (3 marks)

38. The table shows mango 4, banana 3, orange 2 and pawpaw 1. How many pupils did not choose mango? (2 marks)

39. Work out 48 × 21 and check the answer by estimating first. (4 marks)

40. A ribbon is 1 metre long. Write 27 centimetres as a fraction of a metre and as a decimal. (3 marks)

41. (a) Write 3 tenths and 5 hundredths as a decimal. (b) Write 7 hundredths as a decimal. (c) Arrange 0.35, 0.5, 0.07 and 0.29 from the smallest to the largest. (5 marks)

42. A film begins at 4:20 p.m. and runs for 1 hour 40 minutes. Find the time at which it ends. (2 marks)

43. The floor of a shop has 8 rows of 12 square tiles. How many tiles are on the floor? (3 marks)

44. A triangle has two equal sides. How many lines of symmetry does it have? Explain how you can check. (3 marks)

45. Add 3 m 45 cm and 2 m 80 cm. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #11 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — 690
   Look at the ones digit 4. It is less than 5, so keep the tens digit. 694 rounds to 690.

2. B — Thousands
   Counting from the right the places are ones, tens, hundreds, thousands and ten thousands. The digit 6 is in the thousands place.

3. C — seven hundred and eighteen
   718 = seven hundred and eighteen. Say the hundreds, then "and", then the tens and ones.

4. A — Ten thousands
   Counting from the right the places are ones, tens, hundreds, thousands and ten thousands. The digit 9 is in the ten thousands place.

5. D — 2,275
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 6,120 − 3,845 = 2,275. Check: 2,275 + 3,845 = 6,120.

6. B — 800
   38 rounds to 40 and 22 rounds to 20. 40 × 20 = 800.

7. A — 3 5/6
   23 ÷ 6 = 3 remainder 5. The whole number is 3 and the fraction is 5/6, so 23/6 = 3 5/6.

8. A — 0.04
   Give every number the same number of decimal places and compare from the left. The smallest number is 0.04.

9. A — 0.70
   Adding a zero at the end of a decimal does not change its value. 0.7 = 0.70.

10. C — 0.07
   7 out of 100 squares is 7/100 = 0.07.

11. B — 20 − n
   The key words tell us the operation. "n subtracted from 20" is written 20 − n.

12. C — 2 m 40 cm
   960 ÷ 4 = 240 cm = 2 m 40 cm.

13. D — 6 m 20 cm
   Change to centimetres: 290 + 330 = 620 cm = 6 m 20 cm.

14. D — 7 cm
   Subtract the start from the end: 9 − 2 = 7 cm.

15. B — 300 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. 3 × 100 = 300. So the answer is 300 cm.

16. A — 27 blocks
   One layer has 3 × 3 = 9 blocks. There are 3 layers, so the volume is 9 × 3 = 27 blocks.

17. A — Make one flat layer with rows and columns
   We build one layer first and then add more layers on top.

18. D — 80 blocks
   Volume = blocks in one layer × layers = 20 × 4 = 80 blocks.

19. A — 3
   Layers = 72 ÷ 24 = 3.

20. C — 7 1/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 4 1/2 kg + 2 3/4 kg = 7 1/4 kg.

21. D — Kilogram
   Mass is measured in kilograms.

22. D — 720 minutes
   1 hour = 60 minutes, so 12 × 60 = 720 minutes.

23. A — 120 hours
   1 day = 24 hours, so 5 × 24 = 120 hours.

24. C — 4 h 30 min
   270 ÷ 60 = 4 remainder 30, so 270 minutes = 4 h 30 min.

25. A — 2 h 30 min
   Change 1 hour to 60 minutes when the minutes are not enough. The answer is 2 h 30 min.

26. C — 300 cents
   Ksh 1 = 100 cents, so Ksh 3 = 3 × 100 = 300 cents.

27. A — Ksh 3.25
   325 ÷ 100 = 3 remainder 25, so it is Ksh 3.25.

28. C — 10
   Add all the numbers: 5 + 3 + 1 + 1 = 10.

29. A — 12
   2 × 5 + 2 = 12.

30. A — across the page
   Rows go across and columns go down.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with 3 rows of 5 squares; area = 15 square units.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 3 rows, 1 mark for 5 columns, 1 mark for area 15.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Right angle: 3 o'clock (or 9 o'clock). Straight line: 6 o'clock.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for a right angle example and reason, 2 marks for a straight line example and reason.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: 3 × 8 = 24, 8 × 3 = 24, 24 ÷ 3 = 8, 24 ÷ 8 = 3
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct fact.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: 4 buckets; 20 cups
   Working / marking points: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 (2 marks); 5 × 4 = 20 cups (2 marks).

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: 11/4 = 2 3/4. Check: 2 × 4 = 8 and 8 + 3 = 11, so 11/4.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for 2 3/4 with working, 2 marks for the correct check.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Perimeter = 8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 26 cm.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a labelled rectangle, 1 mark for adding all four sides, 1 mark for 26 cm.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 7.99, Ksh 8.05, Ksh 8.25, Ksh 8.50
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 7.99 first and 2 marks for the correct order of the rest.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: 6 pupils
   Working / marking points: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 pupils; 10 − 4 = 6 (1 mark for the total, 1 mark for the answer).

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate 50 × 20 = 1,000. Exact: 48 × 1 = 48 and 48 × 20 = 960, so 1,008.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the estimate, 1 mark for each partial product and 1 mark for the sum 1,008.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: 27/100 m = 0.27 m
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying 1 m = 100 cm, 1 mark for 27/100, 1 mark for 0.27.

41. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 0.35 (b) 0.07 (c) 0.07, 0.29, 0.35, 0.5
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for (a), 1 mark for (b), 3 marks for (c) (0.07 first, 0.5 last, and the middle two in order).

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: 6:00 p.m.
   Working / marking points: 4:20 + 1 h = 5:20 p.m. (1 mark); + 40 min = 6:00 p.m. (1 mark).

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: 96 tiles
   Working / marking points: 8 × 12 (1 mark); 80 + 16 (1 mark); 96 tiles (1 mark).

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: One line of symmetry. Fold it from the top corner to the middle of the base and the two halves match.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for one, 1 mark for the fold, 1 mark for the halves matching.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: 6 m 25 cm
   Working / marking points: 345 + 280 = 625 cm (2 marks); 625 cm = 6 m 25 cm (1 mark).
